podcast.title: Background and Role in Roxy Music
podcast.body: Brian Ferry was the frontman for Roxy Music, which he helped form in 1970 as an experimental art rock band. Prior to this, he had been fired from a job teaching ceramics at a girl's school. "an out front was Brian Ferry, who had just been fired from his job teaching ceramics at a girl's school."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Dating Life
podcast.body: When Brian Ferry was 61 years old, he dated a 27-year-old model who had previously dated his son, Otis Ferry. "When dad was 61, he dated a 27 year old model. What was interesting was that model once dated Otis."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Iconic Band Leader
podcast.body: Brian Ferry was the legendary leader of Roxy Music, recognized as one of the most stylish British bands of the mid to late 1970s. Roxy Music sold numerous records and provided inspiration to millions, often appealing to fans of David Bowie. "Brian Ferry was the legendary leader of Roxy Music, one of the most stylish of all the British bands of the middle and late 70s."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Rock Star Kids ｜ From the Archives

podcast.title: Rejected "Don't You (Forget About Me)"
podcast.body: Brian Ferry of Roxy Music was the first artist approached to record the song "Don't You (Forget About Me)" for *The Breakfast Club* soundtrack, but he disliked it and turned it down. The song, written by Keith Forsey with Ferry initially in mind, went on to become a massive hit for Simple Minds after several other artists also rejected it. "Kelsey wrote a song with Roxy Music's Brian Ferry in mind, but Ferry didn't like it and turned it down."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Formation and Early Struggles
xref.body: Roxy Music was formed in 1970 as an experimental art rock outfit, with Brian Ferry fronting the band after being fired from his job teaching ceramics. After a slow start, they secured a record deal in 1971. "They were formed as an experimental art rock outfit in 1970, an out front was Brian Ferry, who had just been fired from his job teaching ceramics at a girl's school."

xref.title: Pro Fox Hunting Activist
xref.body: Charles Frederick Otis Ferry, son of Brian Ferry, is an activist known for his strong support of fox hunting, viewing it as a traditional practice within the United Kingdom. He has actively campaigned against attempts to ban the aristocratic sport in Britain, which considers it cruel and inhumane. "See, Otis loves fox hunting. You know the aristocratic sport of tracking down a poor little fox with a team of horses and a pack of hounds?"

xref.title: Rejected "Don't You (Forget About Me)"
xref.body: Billy Idol was approached to record the song "Don't You (Forget About Me)" for *The Breakfast Club* soundtrack but ultimately turned it down. The song was initially written by Keith Forsey with Brian Ferry in mind, and after Idol's rejection, it eventually found its way to Simple Minds, becoming their biggest hit. "Then Forsy approached Billy Idle to record the song for the movie. He turned it down."
